title: Understanding LLM Performance Degradation in Multi-Instance Processing: The Roles of Instance Count and Context Length
abstract: arXiv:2603.22608v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Users often rely on Large Language Models (LLMs) for processing multiple documents or performing analysis over a number of instances. For example, analysing the overall sentiment of a number of movie reviews requires an LLM to process the sentiment of each review individually in order to provide a final aggregated answer. While LLM performance on such individual tasks is generally high, there has been little research on how LLMs perform when dealing with multi-instance inputs. translated_title: 理解大语言模型在多实例处理中的性能退化：实例数量与上下文长度的作用
translated_abstract: 用户经常依赖大语言模型（LLM）来处理多个文档或对多个实例进行分析。例如，分析多条影评的整体情感需要LLM逐条处理每条影评的情感，以便给出最终的汇总答案。虽然LLM在这类单个任务上的表现通常很好，但关于LLM在处理多实例输入时的表现却鲜有研究。本文对LLM在其各自擅长的任务上的多实例处理（MIP）能力进行了全面评估。结果表明，所有LLM都遵循同一种模式：在实例数量较少时（约20-100个）出现轻微的性能下降，而在实例数量更大时则发生性能崩溃。至关重要的是，我们的分析表明，虽然上下文长度与这种退化相关，但实例数量本身才是驱动性能崩溃的关键因素。
tldr: 大语言模型在多实例处理任务中，实例数量较少（约20-100个）时仅出现轻微性能下降，而实例数量继续增大后会发生性能崩溃，且实例数量是比上下文长度更关键的性能退化因素。
en_tdlr: LLMs show only slight degradation with small instance counts (~20-100) but collapse at larger counts in multi-instance processing, with instance count being a more critical driver of degradation than context length.
